plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with slender spikes of small, fragrant flowers above silvery-green, narrow foliage. It is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, peaking in July in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the United States
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray petals around a dark central disc packed with seeds. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky.
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, and the Great Plains of the United States
plants.funFact: The sunflower head is actually composed of thousands of tiny individual flowers arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves that repel water and striking, fragrant flowers held above the water surface on tall stalks. It thrives in warm, shallow ponds and wetlands.
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; grown in ponds throughout India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for over a thousand years; seeds roughly 1,300 years old have been successfully germinated.

plants.name: Eucalyptus caesia
plants.description: A graceful, weeping mallee eucalypt with silvery-white powdery bark and showy clusters of large flowers that attract nectar-feeding birds. It is a rare tree native to granite outcrops.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter and into spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering often starting in late July
plants.location: Western Australia, on granite outcrops near Wheatbelt region; grown in gardens in Australia
plants.funFact: Its flowers have no true petals; the colorful display comes from masses of fluffy stamens.
